Question Choices: Fill: A line is made by placing 5 unit lengths end to end. The length of the line is __ units.
Hints: Count equal units touching end to end with no gaps or overlaps.
Solution: Five equal unit lengths placed end to end give 5×1=5 units of length.

Question Choices: Fill: A rectangle is fully covered by 7 unit squares. The area of the rectangle is __ square units.
Hints: Count unit squares covering the shape with no gaps or overlaps.
Solution: Seven unit squares cover the rectangle without gaps or overlaps. Each is 1 square unit, so area=7 square units.

Question Choices: Select which measurement tells how much space an object takes up in 3 dimensions? ~~Length | Area | Volume~~
Solution: Volume measures occupied space in three dimensions. Length measures one dimension; area measures two.

Question Choices: Two boxes are fully filled with unit cubes. Box A has 16 unit cubes. Box B has 12 unit cubes. Which box has the greater volume?
Hints: Compare counts only when both boxes use the same-size cubes.
Solution: Both boxes use equal unit cubes. BoxA occupies 16 cubic units and BoxB 12 cubic units. Since 16>12, BoxA has greater volume.

Question Choices: Fill: A box is made of 14 unit cubes, each cube is 1 cubic foot. The volume of the box is __ cubic feet
Hints: Multiply the number of blocks by the volume of one block.
Solution: 14 blocks × 1 cubic feet per block = 14 cubic feet. Count every block once; these blocks fill the solid without gaps.

Question Choices: Fill: A model is built from non-overlapping unit cubes, each with a volume of 1 cubic unit. Only 5 cubes are visible from the front. After checking the entire model, you confirm that it contains exactly 10 cubes in total. The volume is __ cubic units.
Hints: Use the confirmed total number of cubes, including hidden cubes. Multiply by the volume of one cube.
Solution: The complete model contains 10 cubes, and each has volume 1 cubic unit. Total volume = 10 x 1 = 10 cubic units. The 5 cubes visible from the front are only part of the model, so that visible count alone does not give the volume.

Question Choices: An object is made of 8 cubes, each with a volume of 2 cubic feet. The volume of the object is __ cubic feet.
Hints: Multiply the number of blocks by the volume of one block.
Solution: 8 blocks × 2 cubic feet per block = 16 cubic feet. Count every block once; these blocks fill the solid without gaps.

Question Choices: Fill: Volume is measured in __ units
Hints: Volume uses cubic units. Choose the size of unit to suit the object.
Solution: Volume measures three-dimensional space, so its units are cubic: units×units×units=units³.

Question Choices: Select which unit is best for measuring the volume of a room: ~~cubic-meters | square-meters | cubic-centimeters~~
Hints: Volume uses cubic units. Choose the size of unit to suit the object.
Solution: A room is a large three-dimensional space. Cubic metres are suitable. Square metres measure area, while cubic centimetres are unnecessarily small for a room.

Question Choices: An object has 3 layers and 4 cubes in each layer. Each cube is 2 cubic centimeters. The volume of this object is __ cubic centimeters
Hints: Multiply layers by blocks per layer, then by the volume of each block.
Solution: 3 layers × 4 cubes per layer = 12 cubes. Each has volume 2 cubic centimeters, so total volume = 12 × 2 = 24 cubic centimeters.
